chief_complaint: burning urination, frequency, and suprapubic pain
hpi_details: A 20-year-old female presents to the clinic with burning urination, frequency, and suprapubic pain. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks she irritated her bladder by not drinking enough water and holding her urine for too long during classes.
concerns: She is worried that the constant urge to urinate and abdominal pain will make it impossible for her to sit through her college exams next week.
expectations: She hopes to get a rapid urine test and a short course of antibiotics or pain relief pills today so the burning stops before exam week.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Acute Cystitis (E. coli) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Acute Cystitis (E. coli) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management favors a short-course, narrow-spectrum oral antibiotic regimen (Nitrofurantoin/Macrobid 100mg BID for 5 days), adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: burning urination, frequency, and suprapubic pain

Key HPI features: A 20-year-old female presents to the clinic with burning urination, frequency, and suprapubic pain. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: Temp 37.0C, HR 78, BP 110/68 (afebrile). Suprapubic tenderness on palpation, no CVA tenderness. Urinalysis: positive leukocyte esterase and nitrites, WBC 10-15/hpf.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acute Cystitis (E. coli).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Pyelonephritis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Fever or flank pain — suggests ascending infection.
management_principles: Confirm diagnosis with urinalysis/urine dipstick (leukocyte esterase, nitrites, pyuria) before starting antibiotics.
Prescribe Nitrofurantoin (Macrobid) 100mg BID for 5 days as first-line therapy for uncomplicated cystitis.
Counsel on adequate hydration, completing the full antibiotic course, and returning promptly if fever, flank pain, or symptoms persist beyond 48-72 hours.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 20F with dysuria, urinary frequency, suprapubic pain, and fatigue, gradually worsening over several days.
reference_soap.objective: T 37.0C, HR 78, BP 110/68. Suprapubic tenderness on palpation, no CVA tenderness. Urinalysis: positive leukocyte esterase and nitrites, WBC 10-15/hpf.
reference_soap.assessment: Acute uncomplicated cystitis, likely E. coli, low risk for pyelonephritis given absence of fever or flank pain.
reference_soap.plan: 1. Urinalysis/urine dipstick to confirm diagnosis. 2. Prescribe Nitrofurantoin (Macrobid) 100mg BID for 5 days. 3. Advise adequate hydration, completing the full antibiotic course, and return if fever, flank pain, or symptoms persist beyond 48-72 hours.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 110/68 mmHg, heart rate 78 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 37.0 C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Young woman appears mildly uncomfortable but is alert and in no acute distress.
Abdomen is flat and symmetric with no scars or visible masses.
Normoactive bowel sounds heard in all four quadrants with no bruits.
Mild tenderness to deep palpation over the suprapubic area; no involuntary guarding, rigidity, or palpable distended bladder.
No rebound tenderness present in any abdominal quadrant or the suprapubic region.
Tympanitic throughout the abdomen; no suprapubic dullness suggesting urinary retention.
No costovertebral angle tenderness on gentle percussion bilaterally.
External genitalia appear normal with no erythema, ulcerations, or abnormal urethral or vaginal discharge.
